use std::sync::{Arc, atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering}};
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Message(Arc<AtomicUsize>);
impl Drop for Message { fn drop(&mut self) { self.0.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst); } }
fn main() {
    let drops = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    let (sender, first) = tokio::sync::broadcast::channel::<Message>(8);
    let second = sender.subscribe();
    for _ in 0..6 { assert!(sender.send(Message(drops.clone())).is_ok()); }
    drop(first);
    assert_eq!(drops.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
    drop(second);
    assert_eq!(drops.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 6);
    assert!(sender.send(Message(drops.clone())).is_err());
    assert_eq!(drops.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 7);
    drop(sender);
    assert_eq!(drops.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 7);
    let lagged = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    let (sender, receiver) = tokio::sync::broadcast::channel::<Message>(2);
    for _ in 0..5 { assert!(sender.send(Message(lagged.clone())).is_ok()); }
    assert_eq!(lagged.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3);
    drop(receiver);
    assert_eq!(lagged.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 5);
    drop(sender);
    assert_eq!(lagged.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 5);
    println!("{} {}", hyper::StatusCode::OK.as_u16(), drops.load(Ordering::SeqCst));
}
